issue: PMAT-204 — a file resource whose PATH contains 666 or 777 could not be applied: bashrs SEC017 reads a chmod line's literal text, so forjar's I8 gate refused its own correct script; the same rule missed a genuinely world-writable mode, which forjar now refuses itself

quorum.kill_rule: a lane verdict is a claim; every counterexample re-run against both the pre-fix baseline (0776fd82) and the branch head before it is acted on
quorum.rounds: q1 width 5 (3 FAIL) refuted the first implementation; q2 width 3 refuters (3 FAIL) killed the redaction rule twice, both reproduced and fixed; q3 width 3 judges (3 FAIL) killed the whitespace-padded quoted mode, reproduced and fixed; q4 width 3 judges (3 FAIL) — none of the seven counterexamples reproduced, five refused at both commits and two accepted at both
refuted_claims: q1: the first implementation's exemption was line-scoped — `chmod '0644' '/srv/a'; sudo -u root chmod 777 /srv/b` and the same with the second chmod in backticks, after `env`, in a subshell and in an `&&` list were ACCEPTED although the pre-fix gate REFUSED every one. Re-run and confirmed; the design was replaced.
q1 lane 4 (/teamwork-preview) PASSED that implementation on the premise that a multi-chmod line is left to bashrs; the premise is false and the PASS is recorded as a review that agreed too early.

q2: `echo \" ; (chmod 777 /foo) ; echo \"` — a backslash-escaped quote re-paired the quotes and swallowed a real chmod 777. Refused at baseline, accepted by that commit: a regression, fixed by honouring backslash escapes.
q2: `chmod 'u=rwx,o=w' '/srv/b'` — a comma-clause symbolic mode was read as safe. Accepted at baseline too, so a hole the new check claimed to close and did not; every clause is judged now.
q2: a chmod behind a backtick or in a subshell was not tokenised as a chmod word by forjar's own check.

q3: `chmod " 777" /foo`, `' 777'`, `'777 '` and a tab-padded mode did not parse as modes, were redacted away with the paths, and turned scripts the baseline REFUSED into accepted ones. Redaction is now restricted to plain path literals.
q4: five of seven counterexamples (a backslash inside single quotes, process substitution, an escaped `c\hmod`, and two variants) are refused at BOTH commits — the refutation did not reproduce.
q4: `chmod 0000666 /foo` is accepted at both commits — a shape neither instrument ever saw, not a regression; closed anyway by reading any octal width.
q4: `chmod $EMPTY_VAR '0666' /foo` is accepted at both commits — the declared undecidable shape (a mode held in a variable), claimed by neither the code nor the CHANGELOG.

crux.verdict: the field keeps the mode in a typed field so a digit-bearing path can never be read as a mode, and only Nix refuses world-writable by construction; forjar now does both — the path cannot speak for the mode, and a world-writable mode is refused at the gate. Third-party figures are documentation memory and marked [X].

agy_teamwork.verdict: PASS — and wrong: it rested on the premise that a line with several chmods is left to bashrs, which three blind lanes and a direct re-run disproved. Recorded as a review that agreed too early.
